newsitem.title: USA: Montana's winter wheat crop nine percent ripe.
newsitem.headline: Montana's winter wheat crop nine percent ripe.

text.p: Montana's winter wheat crop had ripened on nine percent of the acreage as of Sunday, up from five percent for the five-year average, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service reported.
Winter wheat was rated one percent very poor, four percent poor, 30 fair, 56 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Spring wheat was rated one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 36 fair, 49 percent good and five percent excellent.
Spring wheat was headed on 93 percent of the acreage, compared with 86 percent on average. Seventeen percent was turning, against the 14 percent average.
Soil moisture levels were rated two percent very short, 34 percent short, 62 percent adequate and two percent surplus.

Barley was rated one percent very poor, two percent poor, 31 percent fair, 54 percent good and 12 percent excellent. The barley crop was turning color on 29 percent of the acreage, up from the 18 percent average.
Pasture was rated four percent poor, 33 percent fair, 52 percent good and 11 percent excellent.
